articleTitle: Enhancing Noise and Vibration Performance for a Traction Squirrel Cage Induction Machine Through Rotor Design Optimization
abstract: With their durable and simple design, squirrel cage induction machines (SCIMs) have become the preferred choice for electric vehicle (EV) traction application, featuring robust construction that withstands challenging terrains and allowing for cost-effective maintenance, thereby contributing to their widespread adoption in the electrified transportation industry for enhanced reliability and efficiency. Nevertheless, the optimal functionality of the SCIM relies heavily on its electromagnetic design, specifically concerning the rotor geometry. It is imperative to address critical aspects of noise and vibration (NV) in the design process to maximize the electromagnetic performance of the machine, an aspect that was previously neglected. In order to improve the electromagnetic related performance of the SCIMs while keeping the NV aspects at a desired level, this paper focuses on the concurrent modification of the rotor slot shapes of one traction induction machine. In this regard, the initial focus will be on studying the impact of diverse rotor slot and bar shapes on the electromagnetic performance. Subsequently, the electromagnetic force will be computed utilizing the Maxwell stress tensor method. Modal analysis will then be employed to investigate the inherent characteristics of the machine. Following comparisons with alternative scenarios, the machine's optimal performance will serve as a case study, facilitating a comprehensive NV analysis.

articleTitle: Influence of Friction on High Speed Permanent Magnet Bearing Rings
abstract: To build high speed magnetic bearings using sintered NdFeB magnets, it is necessary to assemble bandages with suitable interference by press-fitting. Here we investigate the joining process between titanium grade 5 bandages and sintered NdFeB magnets using finite element analysis (FEA) and experimental measurements with different coefficient of friction. The coefficient of friction, µ, is determined by measured and simulated force-displacement curves. Simulations show that the coefficient of friction between the parts to be joined strongly influences the residual stress in the magnet rings and subsequently the permissible speed of the magnetic bearings.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a New Consequent-Pole Hybrid Excited Permanent Magnet Machine with DC-biased Current
abstract: In this paper, a new consequent-pole hybrid excited permanent magnet machine with DC-biased current (CPHEPM-DC machine), which is applied in the electric vehicles (EVs), is proposed. The unequal teeth structure is adopted in the stator to achieve the excellent flux-regulation capability, in which the teeth can be divided into the main teeth and the auxiliary teeth. The size of the main teeth is slightly larger than the auxiliary teeth. A simplified five-phase multifunctional winding, which can be regarded as both the armature winding and the excitation winding, is adopted. Therefore, the currents input into the five-phase winding can be divided into the AC current and the DC current, in which the air-gap flux density can be regulated by the DC current. There are nine U-type permanent magnets (PMs) and nine iron cores located in the consequent-pole rotor, which are distributed with the sequence of PM-iron. Therefore, both the PM utilization and the output capability of this proposed machine can be increased. The working principle of this proposed machine is introduced in detail. The main flux paths are discussed by the analytical models. Then, the electromagnetic performances, such as the back electromotive forces (back-EMFs), the output torques, the cogging torques and the torque ripples, are simulated by the finite element (FE) method. Finally, it can be obtained that the FE predictions can validate the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the superiority of the proposed CPHEPM-DC machine.

articleTitle: Optimization of Magnetic Properties of Glass-coated Ferromagnetic Microwires by Post-processing
abstract: The influence of post-processing on soft magnetic properties, giant magnetoimpedance (GMI) effect and single domain wall propagation of Co-and Fe-rich glass-coated microwires is evaluated. A notable improvement in both magnetic softness and the GMI effect is observed in stress annealed Co-rich and Fe-rich glass-coated microwires. Annealed Co-rich microwires exhibit a rectangular hysteresis loop. However, higher GMI ratio and better magnetic softness are observed in the Co-based stress-annealed microwires. Single and fast domain wall propagation is observed in the as-prepared Fe-rich microwires. The Domain wall dynamics of Fe-rich microwires was substantially improved by annealing. The GMI ratio Fe-rich microwire was improved by an order of magnitude due to significant transverse magnetic anisotropy induced by stress-annealing. Observed stress-annealing induced anisotropy and related changes of magnetic properties are discussed considering internal stresses relaxation and “back-stresses”.

articleTitle: An Improved Analytical Model for the Novel Counter-Rotating Axial-flux Hybrid-excitation Permanent Magnet Machine
abstract: In order to accurately predict the magnetic field distribution of the counter-rotating axial-flux hybrid-excitation permanent magnet (CR-AFHEPM) machine, an improved subdomain model is proposed in this paper, which combines the Ampere's circuital law with the KCL for equivalent magnetic circuit. Firstly, a simplified subdomain model is established in the Cartesian coordinate system, and the constraint equation considering the excitation circuit is derived by combining the excitation winding and the end of the armature winding. Then, considering the influence of soft magnetic composite (SMC) material saturation, the magnetic vector potential and magnetic density of each subdomain are iteratively calculated, effectively reducing the error of the magnetic field distribution. Finally, accurate prediction is made on the magnetic field distribution and magnetic regulation characteristics of the CR-AFHEPM, and eddy current losses of the permanent magnet are calculated. This model is proven to have significant accuracy in the CR-AFHEPM, providing a novel and convenient method for magnetic field analysis and permanent magnet loss calculation of such machines.

articleTitle: Loss Reduction Method Under Multi-Operating Points Based on Response Surface Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, to reduce the core loss considering multi-operating points, an optimization method based on the response surface algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the mechanism of the core loss of the CP-PM motor is analyzed, and the key parameters of the motor core loss are picked out. This comprehensive analysis of the loss mechanisms, considering frequency, electrical load, and magnetic load, lays the foundation for selecting key parameters and dimensionality reduction of these parameters. Secondly, according to the operation requirements, three equivalent operating points are selected to realize core loss reduction at multi-operating points. Then, the response surface algorithm is introduced to analyze the influence of parameters related to PMs on the core loss under three equivalent operating points. The equivalent core loss coefficient is proposed to establish an optimization function so that the optimal motor design with the minimum core loss coefficient can be obtained. Finally, by comparing the core loss characteristics of the initial design and optimal design, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Assessment of Binder Content and Particle Size Effects on Core Loss in Fe-Si Powder Cores for Broad Frequency Range
abstract: The crystal structure and magnetic properties of Fe- 3.5 wt.% Si (Fe-Si) powder cores, varying in binder contents and median particle sizes, were examined to evaluate the influence of these factors on the core loss. With a median particle size of 10 µm, the core containing 1.0 % binder content exhibited the lowest core loss across a broad frequency range, potentially due to reduced eddy current within the cores. Conversely, with a fixed binder content of 1.0 %, core loss significantly varied with median particle size. The smallest particle size resulted in the lowest core loss in the high frequency range, which might be attributed to diminished eddy current loss. Specifically, a median particle size of 10 µm showed a core loss value of 20.7 J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at 100 kHz and 100 mT, slightly lower than the previously reported 23.0 J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. These findings indicate that by optimizing binder content and particle size, Fe-Si powder cores can be effectively tailored for use across a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Novel Axial-Field Juxtaposed Magnetic Circuit Variable Flux Memory Machine
abstract: To realize the goal of coexisting wide speed regulation range and high efficiency in high-speed operation, a novel axial-field juxtaposed magnetic circuit variable flux memory machine (AF-JMCVFMM) is proposed, which combines the high power density of the axial-field permanent magnet machine (AFPMM) and wide speed regulation range characteristics of the variable flux memory machine (VFMM). Firstly, the topology and variable flux principle of AF-JMCVFMMs with two different rotor topologies are introduced. Subsequently, the main parameters are designed and optimized based on the equivalent magnetic circuit (EMC) and finite element method (FEM). Then, the electromagnetic performance and torque against to speed curves of the proposed machines are compared and analyzed. The results indicate that the wide speed regulation range and the expansion of high efficiency region can be achieved by the proposed machines, which have profound prospects in the field of variable speed traction applications.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Magnetic Flux in Composite Materials Transformer Core
abstract: This paper explores the enhancement of operational characteristics within transformer core designs through structural innovation. A novel composite materials transformer core, comprising amorphous alloys and silicon steel, has been developed to leverage the magnetic properties of both constituents. Prior investigations into such composite materials have primarily emphasized conceptual development and practical application, with scant exploration of the intrinsic mechanisms that govern magnetization behavior. To address this gap, a numerical analysis methodology is presented to scrutinize the magnetization characteristics of the composite materials structure. The study delineates the distribution of the magnetic flux density across the structure under varying saturation conditions. Furthermore, it conducts a quantitative assessment of the magnetic flux variations at the interfaces between dissimilar materials, which can be attributed to their differing permeabilities. The contributions of this research are manifold, offering valuable insights for the experimental design of magnetization characteristics and informing the strategic engineering of magnetic cores within composite materials structures. The findings are expected to catalyze advancements in transformer technology, leading to more efficient and reliable power conversion systems.

articleTitle: Research on the Relationship Between the Distribution of High-Permeability Materials in Rotor and Characteristics of Magnetic Field in Machines
abstract: Synchronous reluctance machine (SRM) has advantages such as low cost and stable performance, however its plenty of structural parameters lead to complex and low-efficiency design. The complex distribution of magnetic barrier in SRM is the reason why its performance is superior to that of machine likes machine with simple salient pole and the above problems. Firstly, the factors that affect the torque of SRM are derived from the perspective that magnetomotive force of armature is modulated at d- and q-axis. The characteristics and corresponding design ideas of machine with different shapes of magnetic barrier and loads are researched based on airgap magnetic field and magnetic field distribution. The relationship between the spatial distribution of SRM with magnetic barriers of various quantities and magnetic field is analyzed and summarized. The parameters of SRM that generate larger and more stable torque and the methods for analyzing SRM are given. The above analysis and effect of improving performance and design efficiency were verified by finite element analysis (FEA) in different 4P/24S SRMs.

articleTitle: Parameter Sensitivity Analysis and Efficiency Improvement of Electromagnetic Repulsion Mechanism Based on Orthogonal Experiment Design
abstract: As a linear actuator, the electromagnetic repulsion mechanism (ERM) has the advantages of simple structure and fast driving speed. It finds wide applications in circuit breakers, bypass switches, and grounding switches in flexible DC transmission systems. However, the low efficiency of ERM, usually less than 5%, remains a significant disadvantage. Although many parameters affect the operation time and efficiency of the ERM, the sensitivity of each parameter requires further exploration. In this paper, a two-dimensional axisymmetric finite element model of ERM is established. Then, 27 orthogonal experiments with eight factors and three levels are carried out through the finite element method. The experiment results and range analysis show that the outer radius of the coil, the mass of the moving parts, and the capacitance-voltage have the greatest impact on ERM efficiency, while the mass of the moving parts, the capacitance value, and the capacitance-voltage have the greatest impact on the 2ms displacement of the moving parts. A larger outer radius of the coil is conducive to improving efficiency, while a smaller mass of the moving parts is conducive to increasing the displacement of the armature. The efficiency of ERM and 2ms armature displacement under the optimal parameter combination obtained from the orthogonal test are calculated. The efficiency is 6.08%, which is better than the 27 parameter combinations. After obtaining the optimal parameter combination through orthogonal experiments, the capacitance and charging voltage are analyzed while keeping the capacitance energy constant. When the capacitance is 2.5mF, the optimal efficiency of ERM is 8.65%, which is further improved compared with the general efficiency of 5%.

articleTitle: Design of a New Consequent-Pole Hybrid Excited Machine with Segmented Stator
abstract: A new consequent-pole hybrid excited (HE) machine with segmented stator (CHE-SS machine) is proposed in this paper. This proposed machine adopts the segmented stator structure to decrease the torque ripple. Two sets of windings, including the armature winding and the excitation winding, are housed in the stator. The stator teeth can be divided into two types: the primary teeth and the secondary teeth. The primary teeth are designed for the armature winding, the secondary teeth are designed for the excitation winding. The permanent magnet (PMs) located in the consequent-pole is designed as the U-shape to achieve the magnetic focusing effect. Several analytical models are proposed to elaborate the operating mechanism of the CHE-SS machine. The characteristics of the major magnetic paths are discussed in detail. The electromagnetic properties of the proposed CHE-SS machine, such as the air-gap flux density, the back electromotive force (back-EMF), the output torque and the cogging torque, are simulated and analyzed by the finite element (FE) method. Eventually, with the help of the FE method, the correctness of the theoretical models and the superiority of the proposed CPHEPM-DC machine can be verified.

articleTitle: Maximum-Torque-per-Watt Control Framework for Variable Flux Reluctance Machines with Magnetic Saturation and Cross-Coupling
abstract: This paper suggests a maximum-torque-per-watt (MTPW) control approach for a variable flux reluctance machine (VFRM), considering factors like the machine's magnetic saturation and cross-coupling between field and armature windings, which are both located in the stator. The VFRM's torque production, which can be highly affected by saturation, relies on the cross-coupling between field and armature windings, and on the varying field and armature currents. The operating points on the torque-speed locus are determined by different combinations of these currents. The paper presents a strategy to obtain the optimum combination of reference field and armature currents based on a saturation-dependent VFRM model with a focus on minimizing the total copper loss, as it is the most dominant loss component for all operating regions of the VFRM. The proposed method is evaluated in both constant-torque and field-weakening operation regions, by employing both saturation-dependent and saturation-independent VFRM model. It is concluded that the adoption of the saturation-dependent model becomes highly critical in the constant-torque region, whereas the effect of saturation becomes insignificant in field-weakening operation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Between Split Stator Permanent Magnet Machine and Flux Reversal Machine
abstract: This paper presents the analysis and electromagnetic comparisons of a new split stator-permanent magnet machine (SSPMM) and the conventional flux reversal machine (FRM). In this paper, the method of PM splitting is provided for torque improvement including PM self-splitting and offset splitting. The electromagnetic performance comparisons of SSPMM with taking different split numbers in self-splitting, various splitting angles in offset-splitting into consideration are investigated. In addition, the operation principle for SSPMM is presented. The electromagnetic performances including the airgap flux density, harmonic distribution, back-electromotive force, cogging torque and steady torque are analyzed comparatively. The finite-element-analysis-predicted results show that SSPMM exhibits the merits of high steady torque, low cogging torque and high torque quality when compared to the conventional FRM.

articleTitle: A Novel Continuously Variable Magnetic Geared Dual Stator Hub-Motor for an E-Bike
abstract: This paper proposes a flux-modulated magnetic geared machine with a continuously variable gear ratio. This motor can be utilized in a wide range of applications, especially in applications where drive torque requirements are not constant. Therefore, in this paper, this motor is proposed to be used as a direct-drive hub-motor for electric vehicles (EV) applications. This topology consists of two stators and a rotor which acts as a flux modulator. The flux modulator (rotor) is placed in between the outer and inner stator. The variable gear ratio has an advantage of wide torque-speed characteristics along with the high power density of conventional geared machines. This paper presents the design considerations for an E-bike applications along with the proof of variable gearing effect. These claims are validated using 2D finite element (FE) analysis and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Ohmic Losses in Composite Material Transformer Cores
abstract: In this investigation, we have enhanced the operational characteristics of the transformer core through material optimization. A novel composite material core, integrating amorphous alloy and silicon steel, has been engineered to exploit the combined loss characteristics of these materials. Prior research on the composite material core has predominantly centered on empirical outcomes, with a limited comprehension of the underpinning mechanisms contributing to its composite loss behavior. This study delves into the loss variations within the composite material transformer core, with a particular emphasis on the eddy current losses induced by the normal magnetic flux at the material interface. We present a derivation of the computational equations for both hysteresis and eddy current losses within the core, accounting for the presence of both amorphous alloy and silicon steel. Furthermore, we conduct a thorough analysis of the variations in normal magnetic flux density at the interface of the disparate materials. The outcomes of this research yield critical insights that are instrumental in guiding the experimental design of loss characteristics in composite material structures and informing the strategic design of transformer cores. These findings are anticipated to contribute to the advancement of transformer technology, leading to more efficient and reliable magnetic energy conversion systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Dual-Stator Permanent Magnet Machines With Harmonic Function Type Inner Stator Teeth for Electric Vehicle
abstract: The paper proposes and analyzes new dual-stator permanent magnet machines with harmonic function type inner stator teeth (HFIST-DSPMMs), which can be applied in electric vehicle requiring high torque quality and high stability. The proposed HFIST can suppress harmonic distortion of airgap flux density to achieve low cogging torque and low torque ripple. The shape of designed HFIST is changed according to required harmonic function, which can be formed as trapezoid- and parallelogram-shaped stator teeth. All of the designed HFISTs can be described using two angles (θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) between three edges in HFIST, which are the key design parameters for the kind and modulation effect of HFIST-DSPMM. Three representative HFIST-DSPMM and the conventional DSPMM with rectangle inner stator teeth are comparatively analyzed using method of finite element analysis (FEA). The calculated results verify that designed HFIST-DSPMMs can offer the performances of low harmonic distortion, low cogging torque, and low torque ripple.

Author Keywords: harmonic function type inner stator teeth

articleTitle: A Novel Winding Design for EV Traction Motors: Hybrid Hairpin Winding Layout Containing Both Copper and Aluminum Windings
abstract: Emerging design considerations for future traction machines call for innovative hairpin winding designs that deliver superior electromagnetic performance across a wider speed range while the motor beign lightweight and cost-effective. To address this challenge, incorporating aluminum as the winding material presents a viable solution due to its lightweight and cost-effective nature. However, overcoming its higher ohmic losses while meeting the higher performance targets remains a critical obstacle that needs to be addressed. In this respect, utilizing winding function-based analytical model, this paper proposed a novel innovative hybrid hairpin winding design layout that combines the integer slot distributed windings (ISDW) and variable pitch concentric winding (VPCW) layouts and validated through 140 kW, 15,000 rpm induction machine (IM) employed in commercially available EV. The hybrid winding layout incorporates both copper and aluminum windings, resulting in a reduction of 36.1% in winding weight and 46.6% in cost compared to the conventional ISDW design made of copper. Additionally, the hybrid winding design exhibits improved output power, torque, and efficiency, over a wider speed range, encompassing both the maximum torque per ampere and field weakening regions.
